newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Scania sets up import company in Russia.
newsitem.headline: Scania sets up import company in Russia.

text.p: Swedish truck maker Scania said on Thursday it would establish an import company in Moscow as of June 1.
In addition, the group plans to invest in a new service plant, Scania said in a statement.
"Demand for our products is increasing markedly in Russia," Urban Erdtman, marketing manager at Scania, said. "Therefore it is natural to create an import company."

Since 1992, Scania has had a representative office in Moscow. Last year it sold 141 trucks in Russia, while total heavy truck imports amounted to 838 vehicles, and so far this year it has sold 160 trucks, the company said.

"The total market for imported trucks seems to be increasing in 1997 compared to last year," Erdtman said. "With our own import company we will strengthen our possibilities to grow at the same rate as the market."
